x-bump-note: 1.0.0 -> 1.1.0 tightened `target_id`'s pattern to reject a trailing '.' (review finding, nit): Windows silently strips a trailing dot from a filename, so `target_id: "foo."` and `target_id: "foo"` would alias to the same on-disk file — a silent-collision hazard on this fleet's primary platform. Classified MAJOR because a value that previously validated (a target_id ending in '.') is now rejected. NOTE: this schema is a PUBLISHED cross-repo contract already delivered to project-opticon — this bump is a narrowing of an already-shipped contract; the EM owes opticon a notification memo, not just a pin recompute.
description: Priority-intent record — the cross-repo contract project-opticon writes against. Modelled on coordinator/schemas/lessons-outbox.schema.json (structural precedent: a drop-directory owned by the consumer, per-entry YAML, drain-and-archive-or-reject, single drainer). The write direction is genuinely INVERTED relative to that precedent: opticon writes INTO this repo's tree rather than into its own outbox, so treat lessons-outbox as a structural cousin, not a fully-precedented shape. The drain (coordinator/schemas/priority-ledger.schema.json's consumer) applies records in `sequence` order, never by file mtime (mtime is worthless on a shared tree), then archives or rejects each one.

target_id.description: Identifier of the priority-ledger target this intent record applies to, same domain as priority-ledger.schema.json's target_id. This value later becomes a filename component and arrives from a process outside our review pipeline, so the pattern strictly rejects path-traversal shapes: no '..', no '/', no '\\', and no leading '.' — only safe filename-component characters are accepted. Also rejects a trailing '.' (review finding, nit): Windows silently strips a trailing dot from a filename, so a target_id ending in '.' would alias to the same on-disk file as the same target_id without it. A trailing space is already excluded — space was never in the accepted character class. Accepted risk, deliberately NOT guarded here: Windows reserved device names (CON/NUL/COM1/...) and a max-length cap — both speculative against an opticon-authored target_id corpus we don't control, and an over-tight pattern on a published cross-repo contract is its own hazard.

priority.description: Requested priority level for the target.

requested_by.description: Identifier of the requester (e.g. a repo or role identifier).

requested_at.description: Timestamp the intent record was authored.

sequence.description: Monotonic sequence number assigned by the producer. REQUIRED: the drain applies intent records in this order, never by file mtime — mtime is worthless on a shared tree (concurrent writers, clock skew, filesystem timestamp coarsening). The ordering rule depends on this field existing; a record without it cannot be placed in the drain's apply order.

note.description: Optional free-text context for the priority request.
